designs.understanding: Reference data is trusted as a whole file. Cards carry review in {base, draft, approved} but no code reads it: 190 of 240 cards are draft (domains_batch2: 70, domains_batch3: 120, all checked) and reach founders unlabelled through agents/tools.py _domain_row/_roadmap. translations.json asks for a per-entry reviewed flag that phrasebook.translation() (phrasebook.py:50-52) ignores. The funding catalogue, pack prices and regulatory items have no per-item checked date or source, so no freshness rule can be stated. Districts outside the five in registry.DISTRICTS read as 'weak fit' because fit() defaults to 1 (registry.py:191-192). registry.load() lets a later batch silently replace a card ({d['id']: d}) and sorts batch files lexically (registry.py:52, :64). The weekly harvest rewrites whole files, so one 'unreachable' erases good records; an OpenAlex budget exit fails the job and skips the PR step; a new dated branch and PR is opened each week with GITHUB_TOKEN (weekly-checks.yml:38-55), so ci.yml never runs on it; and five settled years are re-fetched for every domain. Root cause: no per-item provenance model (source, checked_on, review) with one validator and one freshness helper, and a harvest pipeline that writes instead of merging. All thirteen flags hold against the files.

flags_disputed.note: Describes a planned CI gate (5.2.2), not existing code; the per-entry date gap it found is real (all 46 schemes have no per-scheme checked date).

approaches.name: Per-item provenance block validated by Pydantic models, plus one freshness helper with per-dataset max ages
approaches.how: Every reference item carries provenance {source, checked_on, review, reviewed_by, reviewed_on, checklist}; app/refdata/models.py holds a Pydantic model per data file; loaders validate at load and one test validates all files; app/refdata/freshness.py states the max age per dataset and returns current | stale | never_checked for intake, investor matching, schemes and the weekly report.
approaches.basis: Pydantic v2 is already the stack's validator and can emit JSON Schema for editors (model_json_schema()).
approaches.advantages: No new dependency; the same model validates at runtime and in CI; one staleness rule everywhere.
approaches.drawbacks: A one-time data migration adding provenance to existing items, with honest nulls.

approaches.name: JSON Schema files + jsonschema/check-jsonschema in CI
approaches.how: Write a .schema.json per dataset and validate in CI.
approaches.drawbacks: A new dependency and a second description of shapes the loaders already assume; runtime loading stays unvalidated.

approaches.name: Reference data in PostgreSQL tables with audit columns
approaches.how: Load JSON into tables with reviewed_by/at columns and history.
approaches.drawbacks: Loses diffable data PRs; needs the database on the offline baseline; large change.

approaches.name: Frictionless Data packages
approaches.how: Describe datasets with datapackage.json and validate with frictionless.
approaches.drawbacks: Built for tabular CSV; nested cards fit poorly; heavy dependency.

approaches.name: GitHub Actions hardening: reusable workflow + create-pull-request on a fixed branch + issue-based freshness
approaches.how: data-checks.yml (workflow_call) used by ci.yml and weekly-checks.yml; weekly steps continue-on-error with outcomes recorded; peter-evans/create-pull-request updates one branch and PR; a scheduled freshness step opens or updates one issue instead of failing CI.
approaches.basis: Built-in GitHub features plus a popular maintained action; free for this repo.
approaches.advantages: Checks run on bot PRs without a PAT; one PR to merge; clocks never turn code PRs red.
approaches.drawbacks: Pins a third-party action (pin by commit SHA).

approaches.name: Personal access token / GitHub App for the bot
approaches.how: Open the PR with a PAT so the normal ci.yml triggers.
approaches.drawbacks: A long-lived secret to set up and rotate; still needs step isolation.

designs.chosen: Provenance block + Pydantic dataset models + one freshness helper, with GitHub Actions hardening and merge-based harvest scripts (approaches 1 and 5)
designs.why_chosen: The thirteen flags reduce to two missing things: item-level provenance with one validator, and a harvest pipeline that merges and isolates failures. Pydantic is installed and the loaders already parse these files, so validation happens at load and in tests with zero new dependencies; the freshness helper turns SYSTEM-DESIGN §9's 'last checked on ...' into one function shared by intake, investors and schemes. The workflow changes use built-in features and one widely used action, with no secret to manage.

not_chosen.name: JSON Schema + jsonschema
not_chosen.reason: A second description of the same shapes and a new dependency; Pydantic can emit JSON Schema if editors need it.

not_chosen.name: Reference data in PostgreSQL
not_chosen.reason: Breaks the offline baseline and the reviewable data-PR workflow.

not_chosen.name: Frictionless
not_chosen.reason: Tabular-first and heavy; nested cards fit poorly.

not_chosen.name: PAT / GitHub App
not_chosen.reason: A long-lived secret to rotate for something workflow_call solves for free.

design.components: app/refdata/provenance.py: Provenance(source: str|None, checked_on: date|None, review: Literal['base','draft','approved'], reviewed_by: str|None, reviewed_on: date|None, checklist: dict[str,bool]|None); validator: approved requires reviewed_by, reviewed_on and an answer for every item of the batch's _meta.review_checklist. app/refdata/models.py: DomainCard, RegulatoryItem, PackPrice, Scheme, IntakeRecord, InvestorSignal, DomainSignal, Translation, each embedding provenance fields. app/refdata/freshness.py: MAX_AGE_DAYS = {intake: 14, investor_signals: 30, schemes_open: 30, regulatory: 180, pack_prices: 365, domain_signals: 365}; status(dataset, checked_on, today) -> current|stale|never_checked; label() -> 'last checked on <date>'. scripts/_harvest.py: merge(previous, fresh, transient={'unreachable','timeout'}) keeps the last good record and adds last_attempt + consecutive_failures; summary(previous, merged) for the PR body.
design.data_model: Existing items get provenance with honest values and no invented dates: cards keep review; regulatory items and pack prices get checked_on null and their existing source or null; funding-catalogue entries get checked_on null unless the owner confirms the date. signals.json domains gain checked_on and trend_query_hash. translations.json keeps reviewed. Settings: allow_unreviewed_translations: bool = False. Registry: coverage(district) -> covered | not_covered; fit() returns None for an uncovered district.
design.algorithm: registry.load(): batch files sorted by _meta.batch as int; ValueError on a duplicate id across files; each card validated. Founder wording: _domain_row/_roadmap carry review; the offline template and grounding check add 'from a draft card, not yet checked by a reviewer' to sentences built from draft cards; the model gets review in the tool result plus a SYSTEM rule. Uncovered district: 'I do not have district data for Salem yet, so I cannot say how well this fits there', plus a structlog counter district.not_covered (district only, no person). translation(text, lang): None unless reviewed or the setting is on; callers fall back to English. Investor reachability: stale signals -> status 'stale', score 0.3, 'last checked on ...'. Incremental signals: domains missing, older than 180 days or with a changed trend_query, oldest first, --max per run (default 60); on BudgetExhausted write completed domains and exit 0 with a summary.
design.interfaces: T01 owns vocabulary ids the cards reference; T04 consumes per-scheme checked_on for live status; T13/T21 reuse freshness labels; T22 shares data-checks.yml and the harvest-script tests; T26 consumes the translation gate; T23 shows freshness counts; 5.6.1's reviewer writes reviewed_by/reviewed_on/checklist through the Provenance validator.
design.rollout: 1) loader correctness and validators (data change is provenance nulls only); 2) founder-facing labels and gates; 3) harvest merge and incremental signals; 4) workflow restructuring and the freshness issue.
design.offline: All runtime parts are local file reads; only the weekly workflow is online, and its failure leaves the previous data marked with its date.

designs.understanding: store.py has three stores sharing a four-method protocol and nothing else. Durability, lifetime, read purpose and failure semantics are implied: 'saved' is store.name == 'database' (routers/ideation.py:303), already wrong under CachedStore ('database+redis', store.py:189); one _expired (6 h, store.py:48-49) is applied at three layers, so the Redis copy re-hides a row the database just returned (F-B5-017); the Redis copy is filled by reads with no version guard and delete drops the copy before the row (store.py:206-233), so a slow read resurrects a deleted session; the store kind is chosen once per process (store.py:236-249) and SqlStore has no error handling, so a later outage is a raw 500 and an outage at boot is sticky; and the cohort endpoint reuses the founder's live read one id at a time (cohort.py:40), inheriting the 6-hour hiding and filling Redis with up to 500 copies. Root cause: no contract naming lifetime (cache TTL vs retention), durability, read purpose (live vs analytics) and failure behaviour, with wrappers that delegate instead of re-deciding. All ten flags hold against the code.

flags_disputed.note: Holds, but its recommendation (hold every conversation in memory) conflicts with F-B2-012 (retry, then 503). A NEW conversation can start in memory, honestly marked not saved; an EXISTING durable one cannot continue from memory without forking from its row, so it gets one retry and then a clear 503. Resolved as a combination.
Holds. kept_until depends on decision D4; the lifetime becomes a setting so D4 changes one value, not the message.

approaches.name: Explicit store contract with one lifetime policy and delegating wrappers
approaches.how: Extend SessionStore with durable, kept_until(s), get(id) (live, retention-bounded, no idle hiding), get_many(ids) (analytics: no cache fill, consent filtered) and delete(id). One Lifetime (cache_ttl 6 h, retention = settings.session_retention_days) is the only clock; CachedStore applies no expiry of its own (Redis TTL only) and delegates durable/kept_until.
approaches.basis: Protocols are already the pattern in store.py and results.py; nothing new to install.
approaches.advantages: Fixes the re-hide, analytics and 'saved' flags at the root; testable on MemoryStore and the existing FakeRedis; D4 becomes one setting.
approaches.drawbacks: Touches every store class once; get_many needs a cohort_consent column (migration).

approaches.name: Version-guarded cache writes: Redis Lua compare-and-set plus a delete tombstone
approaches.how: Keep the copy as a Redis hash {v, doc}; one EVAL writes only when no tombstone gone:{id} exists and the incoming version is greater than the stored one, then sets the TTL. delete() sets the tombstone, deletes the row, then drops the copy.
approaches.basis: EVAL is core Redis and exposed by redis-py; atomic on the server in one round trip.
approaches.advantages: Closes the delete-resurrect race and the stale-overwrite 409 across all processes.
approaches.drawbacks: A short script to maintain; the hand-written FakeRedis in tests must emulate it.

approaches.name: Write-through cache only, with delete reordered
approaches.how: Only create/save write Redis; read misses do not populate; delete removes the row first.
approaches.drawbacks: A save landing between row delete and copy drop still resurrects; resumed sessions are never cached.

approaches.name: Resilience libraries (tenacity, pybreaker/aiobreaker)
approaches.how: Decorate SqlStore with retry and a breaker library.
approaches.drawbacks: Two dependencies for one retry and one breaker; services/breaker.py already exists; the fallback itself is still custom.

approaches.name: Redis write-behind as the outage buffer
approaches.how: Keep writes in Redis during an outage and flush later.
approaches.advantages: Existing sessions could continue during an outage.
approaches.drawbacks: Breaks 'nothing is stored only in Redis' (core/redis.py); useless on the offline baseline without Redis; needs reconciliation.

approaches.name: Direct JSONB queries for analytics
approaches.how: cohort.py queries agent_sessions with a JSONB projection.
approaches.drawbacks: Couples analytics to the document shape T34/5.5.5 will change, skips the format upgrade on read, no memory-store path.

designs.chosen: Explicit store contract + Lua compare-and-set cache with tombstone + a FallbackStore that reuses services/breaker.py (approaches 1 and 2, with a hand-rolled fallback)
designs.why_chosen: Every flag is a symptom of callers inferring behaviour, so the lasting fix is a contract that wrappers delegate to. The cache race is a real cross-process race, so only an atomic server-side guard closes it, and EVAL is free through redis-py. The outage path reuses the Breaker class already in the repo, so the store re-probes the database instead of deciding once per process, with no new dependency.

not_chosen.name: Write-through only
not_chosen.reason: Leaves a save-after-delete window across processes and stops caching resumed sessions; CAS + tombstone closes both for one short script.

not_chosen.name: tenacity / pybreaker
not_chosen.reason: Two dependencies for one retry and one breaker; services/breaker.py exists and the fallback logic would still be custom.

not_chosen.name: Redis write-behind

not_chosen.name: Direct JSONB analytics
not_chosen.reason: Couples aggregates to the document format (T34) and has no memory-store path.

design.components: app/agents/lifetime.py: Lifetime(cache_ttl=6 h, retention=timedelta(days=settings.session_retention_days)) with kept_until(s) and retained(s). SessionStore: durable: bool; get(id); get_many(ids, *, consented_only=True); create; save; delete(id) -> bool (T17 adds claim and list_for_owner). MemoryStore (durable False), SqlStore (durable True), CachedStore (delegates durable/kept_until; no _expired; CAS put; tombstone delete), FallbackStore(primary=SqlStore, secondary=MemoryStore, breaker=Breaker('database', threshold=2, window_s=30, cooldown_s=30)). StoreUnavailable mapped to 503 in core/errors.py.
design.data_model: agent_sessions gains cohort_consent BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false (index with last_active), written by create/save like private. Redis: sess:{id} becomes a HASH {v, doc} with EXPIRE cache_ttl; gone:{id} with EXPIRE cache_ttl as tombstone. Settings: session_retention_days = 90 (D4), session_cache_ttl_hours = 6. Responses (start, snapshot, done) carry persistence {saved: bool, kept_until: ISO date | null}.
design.algorithm: CAS put (KEYS sess:id, gone:id; ARGV version, doc, ttl): EXISTS gone -> 0; HGET v >= version -> 0; else HSET, EXPIRE, 1. get: Redis hit returns the doc (TTL is the only cache clock); miss -> inner.get -> CAS put, so a stale read cannot overwrite a newer copy and a deleted id cannot be refilled. delete: SET gone:id EX ttl -> inner.delete -> DEL sess:id. Save conflict still drops the copy. FallbackStore: primary calls retried once after 200 ms on OperationalError/DBAPIError/OSError/TimeoutError, then breaker.fail(); while open, create() goes to memory (durable False), ids held in memory are served there, any other id raises StoreUnavailable ('This conversation can't be saved right now; try again in a minute'); half-open re-probes the database; a memory-born session is created in the database on its first save after recovery, so saved flips true. get_many: one SELECT ... WHERE session_id = ANY(:ids) AND cohort_consent AND last_active > now() - retention; MemoryStore filters its dict; CachedStore delegates without filling Redis.
design.interfaces: T12's end_session calls store.delete and reuses Lifetime.cache_ttl for result TTLs; T17 adds owner_id, claim and list_for_owner to this protocol; T32 retention and erasure use delete/delete_idle and the same tombstones; T20 consumes get_many; T34 upgrades documents inside from_dict on every path; T16 owns the migration chain; Talk.tsx shows the banner from persistence on start, resume and every turn.
design.rollout: 1) durable + persistence field (no schema change); 2) CAS cache + tombstone (old string keys ignored, expire within 6 h); 3) Lifetime with retention, idle hiding removed (value per D4, default 90 days); 4) FallbackStore replaces the once-per-process auto choice; 5) cohort_consent migration and get_many.
design.offline: MemoryStore alone implements the same contract with durable False and kept_until null ('until this server restarts'); FallbackStore without a database behaves like today's memory mode but re-probes every 30 s; without Redis, CachedStore is not built.

designs.understanding: Four process-local maps have no lifecycle: Board.jobs and MemoryResults._rows (jobs.py:58-59, results.py), MemoryStore._docs (store.py:58) and _turn_locks (routers/ideation.py:268). The only removal is Board.forget on the founder's DELETE. Consequences: memory grows with every conversation and idea text outlives the session; a delete racing a running turn is undone because the turn can call board.start and results.put after forget (delete takes no lock, there is no tombstone); and job state is collapsed to a boolean, so wait() returns False for FAILED as for RUNNING (jobs.py:88-92), the founder hears 'still searching' and every turn restarts the failed job (start replaces FAILED, jobs.py:71-73). The stream route takes the lock before the response exists and releases it only in the generator's finally (routers/ideation.py:338-359). Root cause: nothing owns a session's in-process life (start, touch, fail, end). All nine flags hold.

flags_disputed.note: Holds in principle: Starlette normally iterates the body, but a failure between acquire and return or a disconnect before the response starts leaves the lock held; acquiring inside the generator removes the question.

approaches.name: Session lifecycle service owning in-process state, with TTL sweep and tombstones
approaches.how: app/agents/lifecycle.py owns refcounted TurnLocks, Board tombstones (forgotten ids refuse start/put), last-touch per session, and one asyncio sweep task started in lifespan that prunes finished jobs, result rows and MemoryStore docs beyond their TTL; end_session(id) is the single delete path.
approaches.basis: asyncio primitives and the existing lifespan hook in main.py.
approaches.advantages: No dependency; one place for delete races; covers locks, jobs, results and memory docs; gives T32 one call.
approaches.drawbacks: A periodic task to start, stop and test with a fake clock.

approaches.name: cachetools TTLCache / LRUCache per map
approaches.how: Swap the dicts for TTLCache(maxsize, ttl).
approaches.drawbacks: Insert-time TTL, not idle time; can evict a running job or held lock; no fix for write-after-delete or failed state; new dependency.

approaches.name: Durable job queue (arq / RQ / Celery on Redis)
approaches.how: Move jobs and results to Redis-backed workers.
approaches.basis: Standard for background jobs; planned for 2.3.1.
approaches.advantages: Survives restarts and works across workers.
approaches.drawbacks: Redis must stay optional; the offline baseline has none; large change for a leak fix.

approaches.name: PostgreSQL results table with ON DELETE CASCADE
approaches.how: Persist results keyed (session, idea_version, kind) with FK to agent_sessions.
approaches.advantages: Results die with the row; retention follows automatically.
approaches.drawbacks: Blocked on the database being the default; today's memory path stays open.

approaches.name: WeakValueDictionary for locks plus evict on expired read
approaches.how: Weakly held locks; MemoryStore pops a doc when a read finds it expired.
approaches.drawbacks: Covers locks and re-read sessions only; abandoned sessions, the bulk of the leak, stay.

designs.chosen: Session lifecycle service with refcounted turn locks, Board failure states and tombstones, and one in-process TTL sweep; the 2.3.1 results table specified with ON DELETE CASCADE as the durable follow-up
designs.why_chosen: The four maps share one lifecycle, so one owner removes the whole class of leaks and races. It works with no database and no Redis, adds no dependency, and gives T07 (store delete) and T32 (erasure) a single entry point. The failed-state fix belongs to the same object: Board must know a job's terminal state to prune it, so wait() returning the state is the same change.

not_chosen.name: cachetools
not_chosen.reason: Insert-time expiry can evict a running job or held lock and does nothing for write-after-delete or failure reporting.

not_chosen.name: arq/RQ/Celery

design.components: lifecycle.py: TurnLocks.hold(id) async context manager (dict[str, (Lock, count)], entry removed at 0); end_session(id) -> bool: hold lock, board.tombstone(id), store.delete(id), board.forget(id); Sweeper task every settings.sweep_interval_s (600): board.prune, results.prune, MemoryStore.prune, drop old tombstones, apply_erasures() (T32 hook). Board: JobState DONE/RUNNING/FAILED; wait() returns JobState; Job.attempts, failed_at; start() refuses a rerun inside a backoff (60 s doubling, max 3 attempts per session, kind and idea_version); failure notice to listeners; start() and the run() closure refuse tombstoned ids.
design.data_model: MemoryResults rows gain last_access; TTL = Lifetime.cache_ttl (6 h idle), since an absorbed result already lives in the session document. Board.tombstones: dict[str, float] kept 1 h. MemoryStore pruned by retention plus a cap settings.memory_store_max_sessions = 2000 (least recently active evicted, logged). 2.3.1 table agent_results(session_id FK agent_sessions ON DELETE CASCADE, idea_version, kind, payload, created_at), listed in T32's erasure map.
design.algorithm: Turn route: cheap existence check first (404 creates no lock), then TurnLocks.hold: load, turn, save. Stream route: existence check before returning the response; the generator's first statement is async with TurnLocks.hold, and it loads inside. Narration: FAILED research -> one honest line 'I could not search this time; I will try again shortly.' (narrated 'search_failed:<n>'), tool chip status 'failed'; FAILED panel -> 'The review panel could not run this time.' instead of PANEL_BUSY.
design.interfaces: Uses T07 store.delete and Lifetime; T32 calls end_session and fills apply_erasures; T27 uses JobState for its evidence gate; T28 types the failed notice and tool status; T23 exposes map sizes as gauges.
design.rollout: Three small PRs: job states and failure narration; TurnLocks and end_session; sweeper and TTLs. No session-document change.
design.offline: Entirely in-process; works with no database and no Redis.

designs.understanding: Every route under /ideation/agent/sessions/{id} (resume, delete, turn, stream, notices; routers/ideation.py:307-394) is authorised by possession of the 32-hex id alone, and the cohort route takes the same ids (cohort.py:32-41), so a programme holding ids for aggregates can read or delete transcripts. The owner is a free string 'anon' in three places (document, elicitation state, column); the column is written only at create (store.py:148-152), is String(64) with no FK, while users.user_id is a UUID. There is no claim, no 'my conversations' list, and the browser remembers one id per device (Talk.tsx:29). Root cause: no model of who may do what to a conversation. All ten flags hold.

approaches.name: Per-session capability key for anonymous sessions + account ownership after an explicit claim + separate cohort reference
approaches.how: At start the server returns session_id and a random access key (token_urlsafe(24)); only its SHA-256 is stored. Anonymous routes require the key in an X-Session-Key header, never in the URL. A signed-in founder claims sessions by presenting id + key; claim sets owner_id with a conditional UPDATE. Owned sessions require the owner's bearer token. Programmes get an opaque cohort_ref per consenting session.
approaches.basis: Unguessable capability secrets are a well-known pattern; hashlib/hmac in the standard library; FastAPI dependencies already in api/deps.py.
approaches.advantages: Keeps the anonymous start; separates read/write/delete from aggregate access; secrets stay out of paths and logs; claim is explicit and one-way.
approaches.drawbacks: The client must keep id + key pairs; legacy sessions without a key need a transition rule.

design.components: api/deps.py: get_optional_user (None without a token; error only for an invalid token); session_access(session_id, x_session_key, user) -> AgentSession for resume, turn, stream, notices and delete. Rule: owner_id set -> user.user_id == owner_id else 404; owner_id null -> constant-time key-hash match, or legacy rows without access_hash accepted until retention ends them. Store (T07 protocol): claim(pairs, user_id) -> claimed ids; list_for_owner(user_id); get_many_by_cohort_ref(refs). Routes: POST /ideation/agent/sessions/claim (signed in, up to 20 {id, key}); GET /ideation/agent/sessions (my conversations); DELETE /ideation/agent/sessions (delete all via T32 erase_user). Cohort: cohort_ref issued at start when share_with_programme; cohort.py accepts refs only.
design.data_model: agent_sessions: owner_id UUID NULL REFERENCES users(user_id) ON DELETE CASCADE (NULL = anonymous); access_hash CHAR(64) NULL; cohort_ref VARCHAR(32) NULL UNIQUE; the string user_id dropped after backfill ('anon' -> NULL). Session document and elicitation state lose user_id; the store sets AgentSession.owner_id from the column (T34 upgrader drops the old field). Browser (T18 key registry): vanigam_talk_sessions = [{id, key, name, started}] (max 10) replacing vanigam_talk_session.
design.algorithm: Claim: UPDATE agent_sessions SET owner_id = :uid, access_hash = NULL WHERE session_id = :id AND owner_id IS NULL AND access_hash = :hash RETURNING session_id; one transaction; the key stops working after the claim. UI: after sign-in Talk lists this device's unclaimed conversations by name and date and asks 'Add these to my account?'; nothing is claimed automatically; sign-out offers to clear the device list. Programmes receive a cohort_ref from the founder (or, after 5.5.4, via a programme code); it opens no per-session route.
design.interfaces: T14 hardened tokens and identity-aware rate limits; T16 migration chain; T07 store protocol and get_many; T32 erasure by owner_id; T18 browser key registry; T19 cohort consent purpose; T20 disclosure on cohort refs; T28 stream contract (key in header only); T34 document version.
design.rollout: 1) keys for new sessions, enforced where access_hash exists; 2) owner_id migration and backfill, drop user_id after one release; 3) claim, list and delete-all routes plus Talk UI; 4) cohort_ref, old id body accepted for one release with a deprecation warning.
design.offline: Works on MemoryStore (owner and key on the in-memory record); claim and list need sign-in, so offline mode is anonymous-with-key, the safe default.

Choices among cards or levers have no state and no spoken matcher. _convene runs the panel with scan=None (:404-415). The offline path awaits board.wait up to research_wait_s 3 s (+council_wait_s 1.5 s, or opinion_wait_s 12 s) before its first sentence. design.components: app/agents/conversation.py: Pending union, Option{id, label, aliases}, resolve(pending, text, language) -> yes | no | choice:<id> | section:<name> | none, next_pending(). app/agents/choices.py: ordinals en ('first', 'second', '2nd', 'the last'), ta ('முதல்', 'இரண்டாவது', 'மூன்றாவது'), hi ('पहला', 'दूसरा', 'तीसरा'), digits, and label/alias words with word boundaries (T10 tokeniser). app/planner/walk.py: SECTIONS costs, licences, milestones, risks, gates with en/ta/hi keywords and templated sentence builders over the roadmap dict (costs.unit/rows/levers, regulatory titles, milestones, risks_by_phase, gates).
design.data_model: AgentSession.pending (validated dict) replaces pending_slot; the T34 upgrader maps pending_slot -> {'kind': 'ask', 'slot': ...}. WalkRoadmap{section, done, roadmap_idea_version}; ChooseCard/ChooseLever{options, idea_version}. snapshot, ack and done carry pending (typed by T28).
design.algorithm: Turn: resolve against s.pending first; a resolution becomes the action without slot extraction; otherwise observe as today. After roadmap: pending WalkRoadmap; a section keyword or yes/next speaks that section and offers the next undone one; a turn that changes a core, capital or district fact (T03 put outcome 'changed', or idea_version change) rebuilds the roadmap and states the difference ('With the capital now X, the roadmap is N months instead of M.'). Evidence gate: _convene runs only when research is DONE or FAILED (T12 JobState) or not allowed (private mode); otherwise narrate 'I will give the panel's view once the search finishes.', mark opinion_owed, and deliver it from _absorb when research lands; if research failed the brief says it rests on no outside evidence. First sentence: before any board.wait, yield a reflection of a newly understood fact ('So the buyers are mango farmers.') or a recorded ACK from phrasebook.ACKS; waits are shortened once a sentence has been spoken.
design.interfaces: T03 put outcome for revision; T10 tokenisation and negation; T12 JobState; T28 typed pending in events; T34 document version; T26 records new fixed sentences; 1.1.5 and 1.2.4 fill ChooseCard/ChooseLever; Talk.tsx buttons map to the same option ids.
design.rollout: 1) Pending with ask/confirm only (behaviour-preserving, document upgrade); 2) early sentence and evidence gate; 3) roadmap walk and revision; 4) choice matcher when 1.1.5/1.2.4 produce options.
design.offline: Entirely deterministic; the model path reads the same pending state and only rewords.

designs.understanding: Nothing maps a person to their data: every session's owner is 'anon', users -> founders is ON DELETE SET NULL in the wrong direction (models/user.py:24-28), and a Redis copy and the job board survive any delete not made through the app's DELETE route (store.py:206-213, routers/ideation.py:316-318). The retention table keeps consents a year after the data while the erasure sentence deletes them (SYSTEM-DESIGN §5.4). Planned nightly work is an out-of-process script, but Settings resolves .env and the research cache against the working directory (config.py:14, :115), so a root-started script reads no DATABASE_URL and purges a different cache (both directories already exist); there is no run lock and no run record. Root cause: no erasure service, no decided consent rule, and no maintenance runner with a fixed home, a lock and a ledger. All six flags hold.

flags_disputed.note: Holds, but 'run erasure inside the app' and F-A5-028 'OS scheduler only' pull in opposite directions; both are met by running app code (python -m app.maintenance) from the OS scheduler, handling durable stores and Redis directly and in-process maps via tombstones the app's sweeper (T12) reads.

approaches.name: App-package maintenance runner started by the OS scheduler, with lock file, JSONL run ledger and an erasure tombstone bridge
approaches.how: python -m app.maintenance nightly runs registered steps with package-relative paths, takes an exclusive lock file, records each step in a ledger and isolates failures. app/services/erasure.py is called from the CLI, the founder's delete-all route and retention, and writes erasure tombstones the in-app sweeper consumes.
approaches.basis: Windows Task Scheduler and cron are free and present; os.open(O_CREAT|O_EXCL) is a portable lock; JSON lines need nothing.
approaches.advantages: Exactly one run per schedule whatever the worker count; works with no database; missed and failed runs visible; one erasure map for every caller.
approaches.drawbacks: The owner registers one scheduled task (runbook).

approaches.name: In-process scheduler (APScheduler or asyncio loop)
approaches.how: Schedule steps from lifespan.
approaches.drawbacks: N workers fire N runs; needs a cross-process lock anyway; nothing runs when the app is stopped; a dependency.

approaches.name: Localhost admin endpoint called by the OS scheduler
approaches.how: Task Scheduler curls POST /internal/maintenance with a shared secret.
approaches.drawbacks: Reaches one worker's memory only, adds a secret and attack surface, fails when the API is down.

approaches.name: Database-native retention (pg_cron, cascades)
approaches.how: Let PostgreSQL delete and cascade.
approaches.drawbacks: pg_cron not installed locally; blind to Redis, the disk cache and memory; cascades impossible until T17's owner FK.

approaches.name: Hosted scheduler / heartbeat (GitHub Actions cron, healthchecks.io)
approaches.how: External cron or heartbeat monitoring.
approaches.drawbacks: Cannot reach the owner's laptop; hosted services contradict free-and-offline.

designs.chosen: App-package maintenance runner started by the OS scheduler, with lock file, JSONL ledger and erasure tombstone bridge, plus a decided consent-tombstone rule
designs.why_chosen: The OS starts one process and the lock refuses a second, so there is one run per schedule whatever the worker count; it runs whether or not the API is up; the lock and ledger need no database; and reusing app code means paths and settings resolve once in Settings. The tombstone bridge extends erasure to in-process memory without pub/sub. One erasure service serves delete-all (T17), admin requests and retention.

not_chosen.name: In-process scheduler
not_chosen.reason: N runs for N workers, nothing while the app is stopped, and still needs the lock.

not_chosen.name: Localhost admin endpoint
not_chosen.reason: One worker's memory only, a new secret and surface, fails when the API is down.

not_chosen.name: Database-native retention
not_chosen.reason: pg_cron unavailable locally; the database cannot see Redis, disk cache or memory.

not_chosen.name: Hosted scheduler/heartbeat
not_chosen.reason: Hosted and unreachable from a laptop; against free-and-offline.

design.components: core/config.py: BACKEND_DIR = Path(app.__file__).resolve().parents[1]; env_file = BACKEND_DIR/'.env'; validator making every *_dir setting absolute under BACKEND_DIR. app/maintenance/: __main__.py, runner.py (STEPS registry: retention, research_cache_purge, cohort_rebuild (5.5.5), warming (2.2.6)), run_lock() with O_EXCL, pid and start time, stale after 6 h; ledger var/maintenance-runs.jsonl {run_id, step, started, ended, ok, error_class, summary}; non-zero exit if any step failed. app/services/erasure.py: ordered ERASURE_MAP (sessions by owner_id -> ids; agent_results cascade (2.3.1); founder documents, profile, startups; consents -> tombstones; users row last); erase_user(user_id) and erase_sessions(ids) -> receipt; per session T07 store.delete (Redis tombstone) and an erased_sessions row the sweeper applies.
design.data_model: erased_sessions(session_id PK, erased_at), pruned after 7 days. Consent rule (to be written into SYSTEM-DESIGN §5.4): erasure replaces consent rows with consent tombstones {purpose, policy_version, granted_at, erased_at, receipt_id} with no user id, name or contact, deleted one year after erased_at; plain retention keeps consents for the data's life plus one year. Ledger rotated at 1 MB; /health reports last_ok and consecutive_failures per step.
design.algorithm: Nightly: acquire lock (if held, record 'already running' and exit 0); each step in try/except with a ledger line; retention: SqlStore.delete_idle(before = now - retention) -> ids -> Redis tombstones + erased_sessions; cache purge by mtime in the resolved research_cache_dir; release lock. Missed nights: the Task Scheduler entry enables 'run as soon as possible after a missed start' (anacron or @reboot catch-up on Linux); API startup logs maintenance.overdue if any step's last ok run is older than 26 h; 'failing twice' = consecutive_failures >= 2 shown on the 5.4.3 page. Guards: erase_user refuses None, 'anon' and non-UUID values; erase_sessions refuses empty lists or more than 1000 ids per call.
design.interfaces: T17 owner_id FK and the delete-all route; T19 consent table; T30 founder-link direction; T12 sweeper applies erased_sessions; T07 tombstoned delete; T23 shows the ledger; T22's generated .env.example documents resolved paths.
design.rollout: 1) path resolution (fixes the wrong-cache bug now); 2) runner, lock, ledger and cache purge (no database needed); 3) erasure service once T17's owner_id lands; 4) retention step after D4; 5) cohort rebuild and warming register their own steps.
design.offline: Runner, lock and ledger need only local disk; without a database retention and erasure record 'skipped: no database' instead of silently succeeding; the T12 sweeper handles memory-store retention.
